text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Elections for the National Assembly's tenth legislature are planned for July.
-- Economic growth has been maintained during the first quarter of this year with consumer prices increasing by only 2.1 percent, the lowest rise for the period since 1991.
-- U.S Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin is scheduled to arrive in Hanoi on April 6 and will discuss the settlement of debts provided to the former Saigon Regime by the United States.
-- Vice President Nguyen Thi Binh received a French Development Fund delegation on Wednesday to discuss the control and management of co-operation projects.
-- The Thai Prime Minister believes that differences between Vietnam and Thailand on fishing and sea boundaries will be solved positively.

-- The National Assembly spring session is expected to hear reports on the assembly's full term and other reports delivered by the President, the Prime Minister, the presiding judge of the People's Supreme's Court, and the Director of the People's Supreme Prosecution Institute.
-- Prosecutors in the Tamexco corruption scandal appeals trial have asked for the sentences to remain unchanged.
-- On April 1 Ho Chi Minh City will be expanded by incorporating five new districts.
